inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 address the same defect (wallet resubmission ignoring -privatebroadcast) with opposite approaches - route rebroadcasts privately vs. suppress them. They cannot sit in different bands; review #36330 first and decide the policy, then #34533.

Wider rebroadcast cluster: #36398 (only rebroadcast IsFromMe), #36482 (only announce if re-added to mempool), #36330, #34533, #36380 (-walletbroadcast=initialonly) and #36481 (manual rebroadcast) all rewrite the same rebroadcast policy. #36398 is the broadest and should be settled first; parts of #36482/#36330 may become redundant afterwards.
Dependency chain that must be reviewed in order: #33033 (SQLite RAII) -> #33034 (tx table) -> #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXOs). #33033 was scored far below the work it unblocks.

Dependency chain: #36442 (multipath descriptor object) -> #36443 (reconstruct multipath) -> #36444 (store multipath info). #36443 was scored below both of its neighbours despite being the required middle link.

#10102 (multiprocess) is a stated prerequisite of #19460 (-ipcconnect), which in turn unblocks #19461; keep that order.
Multisig wizard (#35645) prerequisites #35918, #36070 and #36143 serve one project and are best reviewed as a block; none unblocks the others.

#35760 and #36638 both change wallet loading to report corruption instead of limping on (rescan loop / assertion crash). They touch the same DBErrors path and should be reviewed together for a consistent corruption policy; #35760 first.
#35998 marks WalletBatch methods nodiscard while #34520 applies nodiscard broadly to bool+out-param getters; overlapping technique, review #35998 first since it carries the fund-safety case.
#36344 and #36494 both harden sendall argument handling (duplicate inputs, unknown option keys); they conflict in the same RPC surface and are adjacent in the list.
#36489 and #36488 are both RPC option-naming changes by the same author; #36489 fixes an actually ignored parameter and should go first, #36488 is pure deprecation.
#36550 supersedes #36551 and #36114 absorbs closed #35358, per their own descriptions - no duplicate review needed.
result.notes: P1 is deliberately small and limited to problems that lose or silently misreport funds, crash the wallet on load, or destroy data on the legacy migration path. P2 is large (31 PRs) because this category genuinely has that many durable fund-safety, migration, privacy and PSBT-interop items; within it the ordering puts correctness and migration ahead of performance and feature work. Drafts and proofs of concept (#33043, #36122) are kept at P3 rather than P2 because the deliverable this cycle is a design decision, not the feature. Test-only and refactor-only changes occupy the bottom of P3 and all of P4, consistent with the rubric's treatment of internally-focused work in a non-cleanup category.
